paper.title: Class 12 English (अंग्रेज़ी - 100 Marks) 2024 Set E (Bihar Board (BSEB))

questions.text: His progress satisfied me. (Choose the correct passive voice)
questions.textHindi: His progress satisfied me. (Choose the correct passive voice)

options.text: I was satisfying with his progress.
options.textHindi: I was satisfying with his progress.

options.text: I am satisfy with his progress.
options.textHindi: I am satisfy with his progress.

options.text: I was satisfied with his progress.
options.textHindi: I was satisfied with his progress.

options.text: I have to be satisfy with his progress.
options.textHindi: I have to be satisfy with his progress.

questions.correctAnswerText: (C) I was satisfied with his progress.
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) I was satisfied with his progress.
The simple past verb 'satisfied' takes 'was + past participle (satisfied)' in passive voice, followed by the preposition 'with'.

questions.text: The engagement party was cancelled as ________ people were against the marriage. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: The engagement party was cancelled as ________ people were against the marriage. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (A) some
'People' is a plural countable noun, which takes 'some' to indicate an unspecified number; 'little' is used with uncountable nouns.

questions.text: Ramesh has been absent ________ Friday. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: Ramesh has been absent ________ Friday. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (A) since
'Since' is used with the present perfect continuous tense to refer to a specific point in time in the past ('Friday').

questions.text: Chicken and rice ________ my favourite dish. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: Chicken and rice ________ my favourite dish. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) is
'Chicken and rice' here refers to a single combined dish/idea, taking a singular verb 'is'.

questions.text: Nadal won all the matches played in Paris. (Choose the correct negative sentence)
questions.textHindi: Nadal won all the matches played in Paris. (Choose the correct negative sentence)

options.text: Nadal does not win all the matches played in Paris.
options.textHindi: Nadal does not win all the matches played in Paris.

options.text: Nadal did not lose a single match played in Paris.
options.textHindi: Nadal did not lose a single match played in Paris.

options.text: Nadal was not able to lose any match played in Paris.
options.textHindi: Nadal was not able to lose any match played in Paris.

options.text: Nadal had lost any match not played in Paris.
options.textHindi: Nadal had lost any match not played in Paris.

questions.correctAnswerText: (B) Nadal did not lose a single match played in Paris.
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) Nadal did not lose a single match played in Paris.
Winning all matches is equivalent to not losing a single match, correctly preserving the original meaning and tense.

questions.text: He says to me, "You are my friend." (Choose the correct indirect narration)
questions.textHindi: He says to me, "You are my friend." (Choose the correct indirect narration)

options.text: He tells me that I am his frien
options.textHindi: He tells me that I am his frien

options.text: He telling me that I will be his frien
options.textHindi: He telling me that I will be his frien

options.text: He told me I am friend of his.
options.textHindi: He told me I am friend of his.

options.text: He will tell me that I will be his frien
options.textHindi: He will tell me that I will be his frien

questions.correctAnswerText: (A) He tells me that I am his friend.
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (A) He tells me that I am his friend.
When the reporting verb is in the present tense ('says to'), it changes to 'tells' and the tense of the reported clause remains unchanged.

questions.text: Do what you want to do, ________ don't disturb me. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: Do what you want to do, ________ don't disturb me. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) but
The conjunction 'but' expresses a contrast between doing what one wants and not causing disturbance.

questions.text: It was not a ________ act at all. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: It was not a ________ act at all. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (D) pardonable
The adjective form 'pardonable' is required to qualify the noun 'act'.

questions.text: Choose the odd one out:
questions.textHindi: Choose the odd one out:
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) Paper
Pen, marker, and pencil are writing instruments, whereas paper is a writing medium.

questions.text: You never have bread and butter for breakfast, ________? (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: You never have bread and butter for breakfast, ________? (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) do you
'Have' functions as an ordinary present tense verb, and the sentence contains the negative word 'never', requiring a positive question tag with auxiliary 'do' ('do you').

questions.text: Choose the correct meaning of: "Out of question".
questions.textHindi: Choose the correct meaning of: "Out of question".
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) Impossible
The idiom 'out of the question' (or 'out of question') means impossible or not worthy of consideration.

questions.text: Their idea of a holiday ________ at a resort. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: Their idea of a holiday ________ at a resort. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) is to relax
An infinitive ('to relax') correctly functions as the subject complement describing 'idea'.

questions.text: He cannot put ________ with such insult. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: He cannot put ________ with such insult. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) up
The phrasal verb 'put up with' means to tolerate or endure.

questions.text: Neither of the two men ________ done this. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: Neither of the two men ________ done this. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) has
The distributive pronoun 'Neither' takes a singular verb ('has').

questions.text: Choose the correct spelling:
questions.textHindi: Choose the correct spelling:
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) Resemblance
The correct spelling is 'Resemblance'.

questions.text: He said to Rita, "Am I ill ?" (Choose the correct indirect speech)
questions.textHindi: He said to Rita, "Am I ill ?" (Choose the correct indirect speech)

options.text: He says that he is ill to Rit
options.textHindi: He says that he is ill to Rit

options.text: He will say to Rita that he is ill.
options.textHindi: He will say to Rita that he is ill.

options.text: He asked Rita if he was ill.
options.textHindi: He asked Rita if he was ill.

options.text: He said to Rita if he is ill.
options.textHindi: He said to Rita if he is ill.

questions.correctAnswerText: (C) He asked Rita if he was ill.
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) He asked Rita if he was ill.
A past yes/no question is converted using 'asked + object + if' and changes present tense 'am' into past 'was'.

questions.text: Find out the ________ things. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: Find out the ________ things. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (D) discarded
The past participle 'discarded' is used as an adjective modifying 'things'.

questions.text: Sri Lanka is ________ islan
questions.textHindi: Sri Lanka is ________ islan
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) an
'Island' begins with a vowel sound, requiring the indefinite article 'an'.

questions.text: They decided ________ the white car. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: They decided ________ the white car. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) on
'Decide on' is the standard prepositional phrase meaning to choose something.

questions.text: My cycle did not ________ brakes. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: My cycle did not ________ brakes. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) have
The auxiliary 'did not' is followed by the base form of the verb ('have').

questions.text: It is time for the bell to be rung. (Choose the correct active voice)
questions.textHindi: It is time for the bell to be rung. (Choose the correct active voice)

options.text: It will be time to ring the bell.
options.textHindi: It will be time to ring the bell.

options.text: Time will be when the bell rings.
options.textHindi: Time will be when the bell rings.

options.text: It is time to ring the bell.
options.textHindi: It is time to ring the bell.

questions.correctAnswerText: (C) It is time to ring the bell.
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) It is time to ring the bell.
The active form of 'It is time for [object] to be [V3]' is 'It is time to [V1] [object]'.

questions.text: He blamed ________ for the ugly situation. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: He blamed ________ for the ugly situation. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (A) himself
The reflexive pronoun matching the third-person singular masculine subject 'He' is 'himself'.

questions.text: We ________ be quiet in the library. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: We ________ be quiet in the library. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (D) must
'Must' expresses necessity/obligation to maintain silence in a library.

questions.text: I would have done a better job ________ he di
questions.textHindi: I would have done a better job ________ he di
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (A) than
The comparative degree 'better' requires the conjunction of comparison 'than'.

questions.text: Ramesh is ________ and hearty. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: Ramesh is ________ and hearty. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (A) hale
'Hale and hearty' is a standard English idiom meaning healthy and strong.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentence:
questions.textHindi: Choose the correct sentence:

options.text: Hardly had he settled into his seat when Radha charged in.
options.textHindi: Hardly had he settled into his seat when Radha charged in.

questions.correctAnswerText: (C) Hardly had he settled into his seat when Radha charged in.
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) Hardly had he settled into his seat when Radha charged in.
'Hardly had... when...' is the correct correlative construction with inversion.

questions.text: He said that he ________ be there. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: He said that he ________ be there. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (A) would
In reported speech following past tense 'said', future modal 'will' shifts to past 'would'.

questions.text: I have not heard of you ________ last week. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: I have not heard of you ________ last week. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (A) since
'Since' is used with the present perfect tense to designate a specific starting point in past time.

questions.text: There are seven days in a ________. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: There are seven days in a ________. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) week
A 'week' is a period of seven days.

questions.text: The police ________ the thief. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: The police ________ the thief. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) arrested
A completed past action takes the simple past tense verb 'arrested'.

questions.text: Akbar was ________ noblest king. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: Akbar was ________ noblest king. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) the
Superlative adjectives like 'noblest' take the definite article 'the'.

questions.text: Moti always ________ chappatis in his dinner. (Choose the correct answer)
questions.textHindi: Moti always ________ chappatis in his dinner. (Choose the correct answer)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) eats
Habitual actions indicated by 'always' take the simple present third-person singular form 'eats'.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentence:
questions.textHindi: Choose the correct sentence:

options.text: He prevented me from going there
options.textHindi: He prevented me from going there

options.text: He prevented me to go there
options.textHindi: He prevented me to go there

options.text: He prevents me at going there
options.textHindi: He prevents me at going there

options.text: He preventing me through going there
options.textHindi: He preventing me through going there

questions.correctAnswerText: (A) He prevented me from going there
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (A) He prevented me from going there
The verb 'prevent' correctly takes the preposition 'from' followed by a gerund ('going').

questions.text: He ________ not be there. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: He ________ not be there. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) need
'Need not' acts as a semi-modal expressing lack of obligation or necessity.

questions.text: ________ the grass. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: ________ the grass. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (A) Keep off
'Keep off' is an idiomatic warning meaning do not walk or step onto something.

questions.text: ________ chair is require
questions.textHindi: ________ chair is require
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (D) An extra
'Chair' is singular countable, which agrees with the singular noun phrase modifier 'An extra'.

questions.text: We should think ________ this matter deeply. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: We should think ________ this matter deeply. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) over
'Think over' means to consider or reflect on something carefully.

questions.text: Choose the correct meaning of : "To read between the lines"
questions.textHindi: Choose the correct meaning of : "To read between the lines"
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (A) to understand the hidden meaning
The idiom means to discern an unexpressed, underlying meaning.

questions.text: Choose the odd one out:
questions.textHindi: Choose the odd one out:
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) Office
School, University, and College are educational institutions, whereas an Office is a general place of business.

questions.text: ________ shall I fear but the ones who hurt me ? (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: ________ shall I fear but the ones who hurt me ? (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) Whom
'Whom' serves as the objective interrogative pronoun governing the transitive verb 'fear'.

questions.text: Choose the correct synonym of 'Forbid':
questions.textHindi: Choose the correct synonym of 'Forbid':
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) Prohibit
'Forbid' and 'prohibit' both mean to disallow or ban.

questions.text: The antonym of 'Duplicate' is ________.
questions.textHindi: The antonym of 'Duplicate' is ________.
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) Original
An 'original' is the primary source, opposite to a 'duplicate' or copy.

questions.text: Choose the correctly spelt word:
questions.textHindi: Choose the correctly spelt word:
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) Consent
The accurate spelling meaning agreement or permission is 'Consent'.

questions.text: They should not ________ upon the poor. (Choose the correct phrase)
questions.textHindi: They should not ________ upon the poor. (Choose the correct phrase)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) look down
'Look down upon' is a phrasal verb meaning to view someone with contempt or disdain.

questions.text: There is ________ university here. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: There is ________ university here. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (A) a
'University' begins with a consonant glide sound /juː/, thus requiring the article 'a'.

questions.text: Rajesh is still shouting, ________ ? (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: Rajesh is still shouting, ________ ? (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (D) isn't he
For an affirmative present continuous statement using 'is', the negative question tag is 'isn't he'.

questions.text: Choose the correct antonym of 'Trivial' :
questions.textHindi: Choose the correct antonym of 'Trivial' :
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) Important
'Trivial' means of little worth or significance, the opposite of 'Important'.

questions.text: This child is very ________ to me. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: This child is very ________ to me. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) dear
'Dear' means beloved or cherished; 'very' modifies a positive degree adjective.

questions.text: Give me something to eat ________ I shall die of hunger. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: Give me something to eat ________ I shall die of hunger. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (A) else
'Else' (or 'or else') presents the negative consequence if the command is not met.

questions.text: All his ________ is stolen. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: All his ________ is stolen. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) luggage
'Luggage' is an uncountable noun used with singular verbs ('is').

questions.text: I bought ________ a shirt. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: I bought ________ a shirt. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (D) myself
The reflexive pronoun agreeing with the subject 'I' is 'myself'.

questions.text: She is very dull. She cannot pass. (Choose the best combination)
questions.textHindi: She is very dull. She cannot pass. (Choose the best combination)

options.text: She is too dull to pass
options.textHindi: She is too dull to pass

options.text: To pass is she too dull
options.textHindi: To pass is she too dull

options.text: Dull is she too to pass
options.textHindi: Dull is she too to pass

options.text: Too dull is to pass she
options.textHindi: Too dull is to pass she

questions.correctAnswerText: (A) She is too dull to pass
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (A) She is too dull to pass
The structure 'too + adjective + to-infinitive' expresses negative consequence concisely.

questions.text: Praveen does not ________ with Mohan. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: Praveen does not ________ with Mohan. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) agree
'Does not' requires the base form of the main verb ('agree').

questions.text: We met a lot of people ________ our holidays. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: We met a lot of people ________ our holidays. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (D) during
'During' indicates the duration or period over which something happens.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentence:
questions.textHindi: Choose the correct sentence:

options.text: I did my work very quick.
options.textHindi: I did my work very quick.

questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) I did my work quickly.
The adverb 'quickly' properly modifies the action verb 'did'.

questions.text: I didn't ________ where he was going. (Choose the correct option)
questions.textHindi: I didn't ________ where he was going. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (A) know
The past auxiliary 'didn't' must be followed by the base verb 'know'.

questions.text: If you invite me, I ________ certainly come. (Choose the correct answer)
questions.textHindi: If you invite me, I ________ certainly come. (Choose the correct answer)
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) would
In standard usage here indicating assurance/modal response (or habitual willingness), 'would' fits the context.

questions.text: Choose the mis-spelt word:
questions.textHindi: Choose the mis-spelt word:
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) Secretry
The correct spelling is 'Secretary'.

questions.text: Choose the mis-spelt word:
questions.textHindi: Choose the mis-spelt word:
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (A) Harmaeni
'Harmaeni' is completely mis-spelt (the accepted spelling is 'Harmony').

questions.text: Choose the correct one word substitution of : "Ceremony of crowning a king"
questions.textHindi: Choose the correct one word substitution of : "Ceremony of crowning a king"
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) Coronation
'Coronation' is the official ceremony marking the crowning of a monarch.

questions.text: The ________ English period is generally considered to be from AD 1150-1500.
questions.textHindi: The ________ English period is generally considered to be from AD 1150-1500.
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) Middle
In the history of English, the Middle English period spans from 1150 to 1500 AD.

questions.text: Latin and ________ were the two major influences on Old English.
questions.textHindi: Latin and ________ were the two major influences on Old English.
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) Scandinavian
Old English vocabulary and structure were primarily influenced by Latin and Scandinavian (Old Norse).

questions.text: The Anglo-Indian community in India use ________ as their mother-tongue.
questions.textHindi: The Anglo-Indian community in India use ________ as their mother-tongue.
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) English
English is historically the mother tongue of the Anglo-Indian community in India.

questions.text: Who wrote 'She Stoops to Conquer'?
questions.textHindi: Who wrote 'She Stoops to Conquer'?
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (D) Oliver Goldsmith
'She Stoops to Conquer' is an 18th-century comedy written by Oliver Goldsmith.

questions.text: ________ stops and hinders our progress.
questions.textHindi: ________ stops and hinders our progress.
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) Poverty
According to the prescribed textbook themes, poverty restricts development and hinders progress.

questions.text: ________ was twelve years old and still at primary school.
questions.textHindi: ________ was twelve years old and still at primary school.
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (A) Seibei
In the short story 'The Artist' by Shiga Naoya, Seibei is a twelve-year-old boy in primary school.

questions.text: Donne compares his journey of life to that of the ________.
questions.textHindi: Donne compares his journey of life to that of the ________.
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) Sun
In 'Sweetest Love, I Do Not Goe', John Donne compares his inevitable return to that of the sun.

questions.text: 'Thou watchest the last oozings hours by hours.' It is from ________.
questions.textHindi: 'Thou watchest the last oozings hours by hours.' It is from ________.
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) Ode to Autumn
This line is taken from John Keats's famous poem 'To Autumn' ('Ode to Autumn').

questions.text: The Anglo-Saxons invaded ________ in AD 449.
questions.textHindi: The Anglo-Saxons invaded ________ in AD 449.
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) Britain
The Germanic tribes (Angles, Saxons, and Jutes) invaded Britain in 449 AD.

questions.text: Wycliff and Langland are writers of the ________ perio
questions.textHindi: Wycliff and Langland are writers of the ________ perio
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) Middle English
John Wycliffe and William Langland were leading 14th-century writers of the Middle English period.

questions.text: Macavity is said to be mysterious because ________.
questions.textHindi: Macavity is said to be mysterious because ________.

options.text: the Scotland Yard is baffled by him
options.textHindi: the Scotland Yard is baffled by him

questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) he has a hidden paw
T. S. Eliot calls Macavity the 'Mystery Cat' because 'he's called the Hidden Paw'.

questions.text: Attic civilization belongs to ________.
questions.textHindi: Attic civilization belongs to ________.
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) Greece
Attic culture refers to ancient Attica and Athens, belonging to Greece.

questions.text: "The past is not dead and static, it is alive and ________."
questions.textHindi: "The past is not dead and static, it is alive and ________."
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) dynamic
Dr. Zakir Hussain asserts in 'Bharat is My Home' that the past is alive and dynamic.

questions.text: "Nanukaka opened his silver snuffbox and took a ________."
questions.textHindi: "Nanukaka opened his silver snuffbox and took a ________."
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) pinch
From Manohar Malgaonkar's 'A Pinch of Snuff', Nanukaka frequently takes a pinch of snuff.

questions.text: Martin Luther King, Jr. wanted the Negroes to continue working with ________.
questions.textHindi: Martin Luther King, Jr. wanted the Negroes to continue working with ________.
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (D) faith
In 'I Have a Dream', King urges people to work with the faith that unearned suffering is redemptive.

questions.text: "The last of the great prehistoric inventions was the art of ________."
questions.textHindi: "The last of the great prehistoric inventions was the art of ________."
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) writing
Bertrand Russell states in 'Ideas That Have Helped Mankind' that writing was the last great prehistoric invention.

questions.text: "Travellers in their last distress" is from ________.
questions.textHindi: "Travellers in their last distress" is from ________.

options.text: Now the Leaves are Falling Fast
options.textHindi: Now the Leaves are Falling Fast

questions.correctAnswerText: (A) Now the Leaves are Falling Fast
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (A) Now the Leaves are Falling Fast
This phrase appears in the final stanza of W. H. Auden's 'Now the Leaves are Falling Fast'.

questions.text: The Soldier is a / an ________.
questions.textHindi: The Soldier is a / an ________.
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (A) sonnet
Rupert Brooke's 'The Soldier' is a fourteen-line patriotic war sonnet.

questions.text: Autumn is a season of ________.
questions.textHindi: Autumn is a season of ________.
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (A) fruitfulness
Keats addresses autumn as the 'Season of mists and mellow fruitfulness'.

questions.text: "And when I crumble, who will remember" is from ________.
questions.textHindi: "And when I crumble, who will remember" is from ________.
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) An Epitaph
This line is from Walter de la Mare's poem 'An Epitaph'.

questions.text: 'Our ancestors, therefore, set a limit to our ________.'
questions.textHindi: 'Our ancestors, therefore, set a limit to our ________.'
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) indulgences
In 'Indian Civilization and Culture', Mahatma Gandhi writes that our ancestors set a limit to our indulgences.

questions.text: "I pledge my loyalty to my country, irrespective of religion or language..." From whose piece is this quotation taken ?
questions.textHindi: "I pledge my loyalty to my country, irrespective of religion or language..." From whose piece is this quotation taken ?
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (A) Zakir Hussain
The quotation is from Dr. Zakir Hussain's presidential acceptance speech, 'Bharat is My Home'.

questions.text: Nanukaka went to visit the ________ Minister.
questions.textHindi: Nanukaka went to visit the ________ Minister.
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (B) Welfare
Nanukaka visited Delhi primarily to see the Welfare Minister.

questions.text: Leep, the dog, was bought for ________ rubles.
questions.textHindi: Leep, the dog, was bought for ________ rubles.
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (C) 85
In Anton Chekhov's play 'A Marriage Proposal', Natalya claims Leap was bought for 85 rubles.

questions.text: In 'Fire-Hymn', Daruwalla talks about a ________.
questions.textHindi: In 'Fire-Hymn', Daruwalla talks about a ________.
questions.explanationHindi:
Answer: (D) burning ghat

questions.modelAnswer:
wer:
a) These lines are taken from John Donne's metaphysical poem 'Sweetest Love, I Do Not Goe'. The poet consoles his beloved by contrasting his journey with the sun's; while the sun has neither desire nor intelligence to guide it, his deep love and desire for her will ensure his swift and safe return.
OR
b) These lines are from W. H. Auden's poem 'Now the Leaves are Falling Fast'. The poet reflects on human life nearing its final, freezing phase of old age and death, where the cold, distant mountain peak represents a harsh ultimate destination that paradoxically provides serene, elevated solace.
OR
c) These lines are from T. S. Eliot's humorous poem 'Macavity: The Mystery Cat'. The speaker describes Macavity as an elusive master criminal who can be casually seen around ordinary streets, yet completely vanishes whenever an actual felony is committed, confounding Scotland Yard.
OR
d) This extract is taken from D. H. Lawrence's poem 'Snake'. The poet experiences an internal conflict between his natural instinctive admiration for the dignified snake and the conventional voice of civilized human education that cowardly demands the creature be killed out of fear.

i) The vast historical expansion of the British Empire, global trade, and international diplomacy established English as a globally dominant and pervasive empire language.
j) The 18th-century grammarians shared the contemporary neoclassical desire for order, rule-governed structure, standardization, and precision in language usage.

wer any three of the following in about 100-120 words:
a) Write the summary of any one of the following poems : i) Sweetest Love, I Do Not Goe ii) The Soldier iii) Now the Leaves are Falling Fast.
b) Write the summary of any one of the following prose pieces : i) A Child is Born ii) Ideas That Have Helped Mankind iii) I Have a Dream.
c) Write a note on the Indian English. OR Write a note on English as a world language. OR Write a note on Modern English.
d) Match the names of the poems given in List-A with their poets in List-B: List-A: i) The Soldier ii) To Autumn iii) Snake iv) My Grandmother's House v) Fire-Hymn; List-B: a) John Keats b) Rupert Brooke c) K. N. Daruwala d) D. H. Lawrence e) Kamala Das.
e) Translate any five into English: i) वे लोग एक स्कूल में पढ़ाते हैं। ii) मेरी घड़ी में एक बजा है। iii) मेरे पास एक सुंदर कलम है। iv) लोग महात्मा गाँधी का आदर करते हैं। v) बिहार की भूमि उपजाऊ है। vi) आपको शिक्षकों का आदर करना चाहिए। vii) वह पढ़ाई में मेरी मदद करती है। viii) क्या कल तुम सुनीता के यहाँ जाओगी ?
f) Match the names of the prose pieces in List-A with their authors in List-B: List-A: i) Bharat is My Home ii) A Pinch of Snuff iii) How Free is the Press iv) The Artist v) The Earth; List-B: a) Dorothy L. Sayers b) Dr. Zakir Hussain c) H. E. Bates d) Manohar Malgaonkar e) Shiga Naoya.
Answer:
a)
i) Sweetest Love, I Do Not Goe: John Donne consoles his beloved on his departure, affirming that his journey is not driven by weariness of her or pursuit of new love. Drawing a comparison with the sun, he reassures her that his true devotion guarantees a swift reunion, concluding that two souls bound in genuine love can never truly be parted.
OR
ii) The Soldier: Rupert Brooke glorifies selfless patriotism during wartime. The speaker expresses no fear of dying in battle, declaring that any foreign soil where he falls will become eternally English. He envisions his consciousness returning cleansed to heaven, reflecting England's landscapes, air, and eternal companionship.
OR
iii) Now the Leaves are Falling Fast: W. H. Auden depicts human mortality, alienation, and social frustration through nature's autumnal decay. Falling leaves and barren branches symbolize human vulnerability to death and the silence of life's vitality, while the distant, snow-capped mountains hold out hope of ultimate spiritual peace.
AND/OR
b)
i) A Child is Born: Germaine Greer examines cultural differences surrounding childbirth, contrasting clinical Western practices with supportive rituals of traditional Asian societies. In traditional communities, pregnancy and child-rearing are celebrated collective experiences where new mothers receive extensive support and community recognition.
OR
ii) Ideas That Have Helped Mankind: Bertrand Russell surveys how pre-historic and historic ideas aided humanity's evolution. Physical inventions such as fire, agriculture, and writing, combined with moral and political concepts like democracy and civil liberties, enabled humans to transcend savage instincts and establish organized civilizations.
OR
iii) I Have a Dream: Martin Luther King, Jr. delivers a passionate plea for racial equality and constitutional civil rights for African Americans. Rejecting racial segregation and prejudice, he envisions an inclusive America where individuals are judged by the content of their character rather than the color of their skin.
AND/OR
c)
Indian English: Indian English is a distinctive, vibrant variety of English developed over two centuries in India. It possesses unique idiomatic phrases, localized vocabulary, and distinct phonological patterns suited to the multilingual Indian cultural landscape. Widely used in Indian education, literature, media, and judicial governance, it has gained worldwide academic and literary acclaim through prominent Indian writers.
OR
English as a World Language: English has established itself as the primary international lingua franca. It dominates international trade, air traffic control, scientific research, higher education, diplomacy, and the internet. Its flexible vocabulary and global reach allow individuals from diverse linguistic backgrounds to communicate and collaborate seamlessly.
OR
Modern English: Modern English spans from 1500 AD to the present day, subdivided into Early and Late Modern English. Accelerated by Caxton's printing press, global colonization, and industrial innovation, it underwent simplified grammar and extensive lexical expansion, evolving into a flexible, globally spoken language today.
AND/OR
d)
i) The Soldier - b) Rupert Brooke; ii) To Autumn - a) John Keats; iii) Snake - d) D. H. Lawrence; iv) My Grandmother's House - e) Kamala Das; v) Fire-Hymn - c) K. N. Daruwala.
AND/OR
e)

f)

Its flexible vocabulary and global reach allow individuals from diverse linguistic backgrounds to communicate and collaborate seamlessly.
